rationale: A clean one-factor-at-a-time swap of the operating leg (cash-vs-soft-capital composition, which had independent positive alpha) into the archive's leading buyback-verified construction, internally consistent and correctly signed, though it remains an incremental permutation of an already-strong family rather than a new mechanism.

Adding dividends to the retirement leg is a coherent "cash actually leaves the firm" generalization and enters in rank space so scaling is handled, but it edges close to the well-published total-payout-yield and net-issuance anomalies interacted with B/M, and the nested SUMRANK silently halves the weight on each payout channel relative to the accrual channel.

NEG(NOWC/sales) is essentially the inverse of the working-capital velocity level already tested in WorkingCapitalTurnoverValue, SupplierFundedCycleValue and, in combination with the buyback leg, inside TripleVerifiedCheapness, so this is close to a strict subset of an archived signal rather than an open design question.

The role reversal is a legitimate and economically meaningful diagnostic about which variable carries the signing, but it is mechanically only a rank/z-score transposition of the leading construction and the resulting spread will be heavily B/M-loaded, so a shrunken FF5 alpha is the near-certain outcome and should be interpreted as such rather than as a failure of the mechanism.

The multiplicative inner term is sign-inconsistent with the hypothesis: the product of two signed, non-ranked terms is equally large and positive for "WC buildup with falling sales" (the intended trap) and for "WC release with rising sales" (the benign case), so the signal conflates opposite economic states.

This is a pure recombination of two elements already tested at the archive frontier plus the operating leg of Proposal 1 in the same batch, so it contributes no new mechanism and its result is largely determined by signals already run or concurrently submitted.
